newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela govt not worried by bolivar appreciation.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela govt not worried by bolivar appreciation.

text.p: The Venezuelan government is not concerned that the Venezuelan bolivar is becoming overvalued government officials said Tuesday.
"The overvaluation has still not reached worrying levels," Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff told a luncheon of the Venezuelan-Brazilian Industry and Trade Chamber.
Petkoff added that the government was keeping a close eye on the exchange rate to avoid an overvalued currency that could hurt exports.
Despite an inflation rate running at over four percent per month the exchange rate has remained broadly stable around 470 bolivars per dollar since exchange controls were relaxed in April.
Central Bank Director Domingo Maza Zavala said the bank saw no need to change its exchange rate policy in spite of the relative strength of the bolivar.
"No changes are planned for the moment. What is planned is to observe the market's behavior," Maza said.
"The exchange rate remains at a stable level. I think this will continue with very little variation until the end of the year," he added.
